title: Fearing Draft and Rising Repression, Waves of Russians Continue to Flee Abroad
snippet: Months after the initial military call-up, Russian citizens are still escaping the country due to ongoing fears of forced conscription and a rapid erosion of personal freedoms.
content:
A steady stream of Russian citizens continues to seek refuge abroad, driven by persistent anxieties over potential new draft orders and a rapidly deteriorating climate for civil liberties under President Vladimir Putin's regime.

Lingering Draft Anxiety

Although the Kremlin previously declared its initial partial mobilization complete, widespread rumors of a second draft continue to alarm the populace. Recent legislative measures in Moscow—including the creation of an electronic military summons system and stricter border controls for draft-eligible men—have fueled fears that another round of conscription is imminent to sustain Russia's war in Ukraine.

Dwindling Freedoms and Brain Drain

Beyond the threat of being sent to the frontline, many fleeing Russians cite an unbearable decline in basic freedoms. An escalating crackdown on political dissent, independent journalism, and anti-war sentiment has left citizens facing severe prison terms for expressing opposition to the government.

This ongoing exodus has resulted in a significant brain drain, with tech professionals, academics, and young families taking up residence in neighboring countries such as Georgia, Armenia, and Kazakhstan. For many, leaving their homeland remains the only viable option to secure their personal safety and avoid being drawn into a war they do not support.
